utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case IT-94-2-I, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Nancy Paterson appearing on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, and with me is Andrew Powell, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Paterson. For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. ILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Borisa Ilic, lawyer from Bosnia-Herzegovina, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ilic. Are you appearing for the accused only in relation to this Initial Appearance, or are you appearing for him for the whole of the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. ILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the time being, the accused asked me to represent him at the Initial Appearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Nikolic, would you stand up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What is your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What is the date upon which you believe that you were born?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 26th of April, 1957.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And what is your present age?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What is the address at which you resided before you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Joakim Vujic 19, Smederevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. Mr. Ilic, it's common practice within the Tribunal for the accused to waive his right to have the indictment read out in full. Have you had a chance of discussing this with your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. ILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means. I should like to inform you that the accused has the indictment in the Serbian language. He has also analysed the indictment, understands all its counts, and is ready to plead identically to all counts of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that a suggestion, a common-sense suggestion, that we should take the pleas globally to the indictment, that is, one plea to all of the counts rather than taking them separately?

utterances.speaker: MR. ILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That is, if I may say so, a very good idea. I'll ask the Prosecution about it in a moment. But before you sit down, are you satisfied that he does understand all of the contents of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, I'm quite convinced. He had enough time to do so, and before today's appearance, I again assured myself that that was the case because we went through the indictment once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that he understands that he does have 30 days within which to plead, if he wishes, but that he may plead today, also if he wishes to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. ILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, he has waived that right and he will plead today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed, for your cooperation. You may sit down. Ms. Paterson, what do you -- what's your attitude towards the suggestion that the accused pleads to all of the indictment at one time?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe our preference would be for him to plead to each count individually, but if you find the one plea acceptable and do a sufficient allocution so that it's clear he fully understands that he is, in fact, pleading to each and every count, we would have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Nikolic, would you stand up again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you whether you plead in the same way to all of the counts in the indictment, and if you say that you do, I will then ask you how you plead to each of the counts in the indictment, that is, from 1 to 80, 8-0, inclusive. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you intend to plead in the same way to all of the counts in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How do you plead, guilty or not guilty, to each and every one of the counts, being numbered 1 to 80, 8-0 in the indictment; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may sit down. Is there anything else that I have to do other than instruct the Registrar about a date for hearing, Ms. Paterson?

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We would just say, for the record, that -- in light of the fact that Mr. Ilic has said that he is representing Mr. Nikolic just for this appearance, we will delay turning over the confirmation material until a permanent attorney is appointed. We are prepared to turn that material over late next week if a new attorney is available, or whenever that occurs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may be that Mr. Ilic will obtain instructions to accept them on behalf of his client anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. PATERSON
utterances.text: If that's the case, we're prepared to provide the confirmation material by the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. The Registrar is instructed to set a date for trial, subject to any further order of the Trial Chamber. In accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the accused is detained until further order. I adjourn.
